ec-153.title: Mashed Fried Eggplant with Garlic Yogurt (Beitinjan Mifassakh)
ec-153.culturalNotes: Recipe 153, page 71 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Slice and salt the eggplants for an hour, then squeeze and pat dry.
instructions.2: Fry them in olive oil until soft and brown.
instructions.3: Mash with the yogurt and garlic.
instructions.4: Stir in the parsley and serve.

ec-154.title: Turkish Eggplant Cream (Hünkar Beğendi)
ec-154.culturalNotes: Recipe 154, page 71 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Roast the eggplants whole in their skins, in a hot oven or on a tray over the stove, turning them when one side softens. Peel, drain and mash the flesh.
instructions.2: Melt the butter and cook the flour in it over a very low heat until golden.
instructions.3: Off the heat, stir in the hot milk, then return to the heat and let it bubble.
instructions.4: Stir in the eggplant, season and cook for 10 minutes.
instructions.5: Off the heat, stir in the cheese and parsley and serve.

ec-155.title: Imam Bayildi with Minced Beef and Yogurt
ec-155.culturalNotes: Recipe 155, page 71 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-155-i6.name: Pine Nuts, Pecans Or Hazelnuts, Chopped

instructions.1: Slice, salt and drain the eggplants, then deep-fry them until dark brown.
instructions.2: Brown the onion in a little oil, add the beef with salt and pepper and cook until its juices are absorbed.
instructions.3: Put the meat and fried eggplant in a pot over a low heat and cook, stirring often, until the eggplant has completely broken down.
instructions.4: Press the mixture against the side of the pot with a wooden spoon to squeeze out excess fat, and pour it off.
instructions.5: Spread in a shallow dish. Mix the yogurt with the garlic and a little salt and spread it over the top.
instructions.6: Sprinkle with the nuts and serve hot or cold.

ec-158.title: Imam Bayildi: Baked Eggplant Shells with Currants
ec-158.culturalNotes: Recipe 158, page 73 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the currants in lukewarm water.
instructions.2: Halve the eggplants lengthwise and scoop out the flesh without piercing the skins. Dice or mash the flesh and sprinkle it with lemon juice.
instructions.3: Fry the eggplant flesh with the onions in the oil, then add the tomatoes, parsley, thyme, bay leaf, salt and pepper. Cover and cook over a low heat for about 20 minutes.
instructions.4: Off the heat, stir in the garlic and the drained currants.
instructions.5: Arrange the eggplant shells in a well-greased baking dish and fill them with the mixture.
instructions.6: Drizzle a little olive oil over each and bake in a slow oven until the shells are soft.

ec-161.title: Poached Fish Sayadiya with Brown Onion Rice (Sayadiyit al-Samak)
ec-161.culturalNotes: Recipe 161, page 74 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Fry the onion in the oil until deep brown.
instructions.2: Add about 2 cups of water with salt and pepper and bring to the boil.
instructions.3: Add the fish and poach over a low heat for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Strain the broth, top it up with water and use it to cook the rice (fry the rice briefly in a little oil first, then simmer until the liquid is absorbed).
instructions.5: Skin, bone and flake the fish and fold it through the rice.

ec-164.title: Fried Fish Sayadiya (Sayadiyit Samak Ma’li)
ec-164.culturalNotes: Recipe 164, page 75 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the fish into neat pieces, fry them and drain on absorbent paper.
instructions.2: Fry the onion in the same oil until deep brown.
instructions.3: Add the rice and water with salt and cook uncovered until the water has been absorbed.
instructions.4: Lay the fried fish on top of the rice, turn the heat to its lowest, cover and cook for 15–20 minutes.
instructions.5: Serve the fish on its rice.

ec-167.title: Fish and Vegetables Baked in Tahini (Samak bi-l-Khudar wi-l-Tahina)
ec-167.culturalNotes: Recipe 167, page 76 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-167-i5.name: Sweet Peppers, Seeded And Thinly Sliced

ec-167-i7.name: Tahini Sauce (tahini Thinned With Water, Lemon, Vinegar, Cumin And Salt)

instructions.1: Cut the fish into large chunks, coat them in seasoned flour and fry. Drain, cool and flake.
instructions.2: Parboil the carrots and slice them thinly.
instructions.3: Sauté the onions and sweet peppers and mix them into the fish with the carrots and eggs.
instructions.4: Spread the mixture in a baking pan and cover it with the tahini sauce.
instructions.5: Bake in the middle of a moderate, preheated oven for 15 minutes.

ec-177.title: Gulf-Style Baked Fish with Tomato and Tamarind (Samak bi Salsat al-Tamata wal-Sabbar)
ec-177.culturalNotes: Recipe 177, page 81 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-177-i3.name: Tamarind (soaked And Strained To 1/2 Cup Concentrate)

instructions.1: Split the fish lengthwise from head to tail and open it out like a book.
instructions.2: Dissolve the tomato paste in the tamarind liquid and set aside.
instructions.3: Blend the garlic, lemon juice, mixed spice and half the fresh coriander. Rub half of this mixture over the fish and leave it to rest.
instructions.4: Lay the fish on an oiled baking tray and bake until cooked through.
instructions.5: Meanwhile, fry the onions and peppers in olive oil until soft, then stir in the ground coriander, cumin, ginger and salt.
instructions.6: Spread the onion mixture and the diced tomatoes over the baked fish, scatter over the remaining coriander and pour the tamarind sauce on top.
instructions.7: Return to the oven for 5–7 minutes so the fish takes on the flavours, then serve.

ec-178.title: Tunisian Breaded Fish in Spicy Tomato Sauce (Hout Moqly)
ec-178.culturalNotes: Recipe 178, page 81 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Marinate the fish in the lemon juice and salt.
instructions.2: Fry the onions and zucchini lightly in olive oil, then add the garlic, harissa, salt, pepper and the tomato paste thinned with 1 cup of water. Cook for 15 minutes.
instructions.3: Mash the sauce and boil it again until reduced and thick.
instructions.4: Dip the fish in beaten egg, coat with breadcrumbs and deep-fry.
instructions.5: Arrange on a serving dish and spoon the tomato sauce over.

ec-179.title: Tunisian Grilled Fish with Eggplant Sauce (Sharmoulit Badinjan)
ec-179.culturalNotes: Recipe 179, page 82 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Slice, salt and drain the eggplants, then fry them in olive oil until dark brown.
instructions.2: Grill the fish and keep it warm.
instructions.3: Brown the onions in the eggplant oil, add the garlic, harissa, tabil and the tomato paste thinned with 1 cup of water, and cook over a medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring often.
instructions.4: Mash the eggplant with the vinegar and some salt and stir it into the tomato sauce. Cook for 3–5 minutes more.
instructions.5: Pour the sauce over the grilled fish and serve.

ec-180.title: Jordanian Sayadiyeh (Fish in Dark Onion Broth with Rice)
ec-180.culturalNotes: Recipe 180, page 82 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Marinate the fish in the lemon juice and salt for 1–2 hours.
instructions.2: Fry the onions until very brown, then add the garlic and fry, stirring constantly so it does not stick.
instructions.3: Take the pan off the heat and mash the onions well with the back of a spoon. Add the spices, seasoning and plenty of water.
instructions.4: Bring back to the boil, add the fish and cook until tender. The broth should be very dark.
instructions.5: Keep back just enough broth to cover the fish. Fry the rice in oil until every grain is coated, add broth to make 1 1/2 times the volume of the rice, season and cook until tender.
instructions.6: Serve the rice and the fish in its broth separately.

ec-181.title: Iraqi Baked Fish Stuffed with Walnuts and Pomegranate (Samaka Harra)
ec-181.culturalNotes: Recipe 181, page 83 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the bulgur for an hour.
instructions.2: Pound or blend the bulgur with the garlic, onions, walnuts, parsley, coriander, lemon juice and salt until well mixed.
instructions.3: Stir in the pomegranate seeds and stuff the fish with the mixture.
instructions.4: Put the fish and any extra stuffing in a well-oiled baking dish and cover with foil.
instructions.5: Bake in a hot, preheated oven for 30 minutes, then lower to moderate and bake for 30 minutes more.

ec-183.title: Spiced Boiled Gizzards with Mastic (‘Awanis Maslu’a)
ec-183.culturalNotes: Recipe 183, page 84 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Tie the mastic and cardamom in a muslin bag.
instructions.2: Boil 4–5 cups of water with the spice bag, the onion and salt.
instructions.3: Add the gizzards and cook for 10–12 minutes.
instructions.4: Use the gizzards in the dishes that follow, and the broth to cook rice or vermicelli.

ec-184.title: Gizzards and Pearl Onions Baked in Béchamel (‘Awanis bi-l-Bechamel)
ec-184.culturalNotes: Recipe 184, page 84 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Boil the gizzards with mastic, cardamom and onion as in the spiced boiled gizzards recipe.
instructions.2: Peel the pearl onions, leaving them whole, parboil in salted water and drain.
instructions.3: Halve the gizzards and put them in a deep baking dish with the onions.
instructions.4: Stir the nutmeg into the béchamel and pour it over.
instructions.5: Bake in a moderate, preheated oven for 20 minutes, until the top is browned.

ec-185.title: Gizzard and Vegetable Casserole (Tagin ‘Awanis)
ec-185.culturalNotes: Recipe 185, page 84 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Parboil the carrots, potatoes and peas in salted water and drain. Slice the carrots thinly and dice the potatoes.
instructions.2: Put the vegetables and gizzards in a casserole.
instructions.3: Stir the cornflour and mixed spices into the well-seasoned gizzard broth and pour it over.
instructions.4: Bake in a moderate, preheated oven for 30–40 minutes.

ec-186.title: Gizzards in Tomato Sauce (‘Awanis bi-l-Dim‘a)
ec-186.culturalNotes: Recipe 186, page 85 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Tomato sauce: soften the onions in oil, add the garlic and fry until pale brown, then add the tomato juice and simmer for 15–20 minutes until dark. Add the vinegar, salt and pepper and cook for 2–3 minutes.
instructions.2: Halve the gizzards and parboil them for 3–5 minutes, then drain.
instructions.3: Add them to the tomato sauce with the mixed spice.
instructions.4: Simmer over a very low heat for 20–30 minutes.

ec-189.title: Freekeh with Gizzards (Firik Matbukh bi-l-‘Awanis)
ec-189.culturalNotes: Recipe 189, page 86 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Clean the freekeh: rub it in a bowl of water so the chaff floats and grit sinks, and rinse until the water runs clear.
instructions.2: Bring the gizzard broth to the boil, topped up with water to make 5 cups.
instructions.3: Add the freekeh and cook for 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Halve the gizzards and mix them into the freekeh.
instructions.5: Pour the melted butter over and cook over a very low heat for 10–15 minutes more, until the freekeh is soft.

ec-191.title: Fried Beef Head Meat (Lahmit al-Ras Ma’liya)
ec-191.culturalNotes: Recipe 191, page 87 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Blanch the meat and drain it (head meat is always sold boned).
instructions.2: Return it to the pot with the chopped onion, peppercorns, salt and just enough water to cover, and cook until tender.
instructions.3: Drain the meat and fry it in the oil.
instructions.4: Strain the stock, thicken it with the cornflour and serve it in a separate bowl.

ec-192.title: Braised Beef Head Meat (Lahmit al-Ras Matbukha)
ec-192.culturalNotes: Recipe 192, page 87 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Rub the onion with salt, pepper and mixed spice.
instructions.2: Put it in a pot with the meat and oil and cook over a very low heat until the meat has reabsorbed the juices it releases.
instructions.3: Add a little water, and more whenever it dries out, and cook until the meat is tender, about 45 minutes.

ec-194.title: Jellied Sheep’s Head Terrine (Jilatin al-Ras)
ec-194.culturalNotes: Recipe 194, page 88 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-194-i9.name: Egg (whole, With Its Crushed Shell, To Clear The Stock)

instructions.1: Have the skull split lengthwise. Soak it in several changes of salted water, singe off any hairs and scrape it with a blunt knife, then wash under running water and blanch.
instructions.2: Remove the brain and keep it for another dish.
instructions.3: Simmer the head over a very low heat for 2–3 hours with the onion, carrot, celery, cardamom, bay leaf, peppercorns, lemon rind and the whole egg (yolk, white and crushed shell).
instructions.4: Strain the stock, season it and set aside.
instructions.5: Cut the meat and tongue into small, even pieces.
instructions.6: Cook the peas and diced carrots in salted water until soft, drain, cool and mix with the chopped pickles.
instructions.7: Line the bottom of a cake mould with meat, cover with the vegetables and finish with another layer of meat.
instructions.8: Pour the stock over and leave to cool. When the jelly has set, turn it out onto a serving dish.

ec-196.title: Braised Heart with Garlic (‘Alb Misabbik)
ec-196.culturalNotes: Recipe 196, page 89 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-196-i2.name: Garlic Cloves, Peeled And Halved Diagonally

instructions.1: Slice the heart and soak it in salted water for 1–2 hours. Rinse in several changes of water, gently squeezing out the blood.
instructions.2: Cook the slices over a low heat, stirring often, until they give up their juice, then drain.
instructions.3: Fry the heart and garlic lightly in the oil and season.
instructions.4: Cover with meat stock and simmer for 30–40 minutes.
instructions.5: In tomato sauce (recipe 197 in the book): use 2–3 cups of tomato sauce instead of the stock.

ec-201.title: Kidneys in Nutmeg Gravy (Kalawi Matbukha)
ec-201.culturalNotes: Recipe 201, page 90 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Remove the skin and fat from the kidneys, cut them into walnut-sized pieces and soak in several changes of salted water for at least an hour. Drain and pat dry.
instructions.2: Sauté the onions in oil, add the kidneys and fry, stirring now and then, until their juices are absorbed.
instructions.3: Add the stock with salt and pepper and cook for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Lift the kidneys onto a warm dish.
instructions.5: Thicken the pan juices with the cornflour, add the nutmeg, check the seasoning and pour over the kidneys.

ec-208.title: Mujaddara (Brown Lentils and Rice with Fried Onions)
ec-208.culturalNotes: Recipe 208, page 94 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cover the lentils with twice their volume of water and boil until almost done.
instructions.2: Add the rice and salt, stir, cover and cook for about 15 minutes, until both lentils and rice are tender.
instructions.3: Fry the onions until deep brown.
instructions.4: Tip the onions and their oil into the lentils, stir and simmer for 5 minutes more.
instructions.5: Serve hot or cold. It should be soft, like a thick porridge.

ec-213.title: Turkish Fried Liver with Spring Onion and Parsley (Ciğer Tava)
ec-213.culturalNotes: Recipe 213, page 95 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the liver in salted water for 30 minutes, drain, pat dry and cut into 3 cm cubes.
instructions.2: Coat the cubes in seasoned flour and fry until nicely browned, taking care not to overcook them.
instructions.3: Season, scatter over the spring onions and parsley and toss together.

ec-214.title: Yemeni Liver and Kidney Stew (Kirsheh)
ec-214.culturalNotes: Recipe 214, page 95 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Wash and skin the kidney, chop it coarsely and soak in several changes of water. Drain and pat dry. Cut the liver into small cubes.
instructions.2: Pound the garlic with the turmeric, cumin, coriander and cardamom into a thick paste.
instructions.3: Fry the kidney in oil, stirring, until its juices have been absorbed or evaporated, then lift it out.
instructions.4: Soften the onions in the same oil, lower the heat right down, add the ginger and garlic paste and cook for 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
instructions.5: Return the kidney, turn up the heat, add the liver and cook for 7–10 minutes, still stirring.
instructions.6: When the liver is browned, add the tomatoes with salt and pepper and cook for about 5 minutes, until the tomatoes are done.

ec-216.title: Beef with Garlic and Coriander (Kuzbariyit al-Lahma)
ec-216.culturalNotes: Recipe 216, page 97 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Crush the garlic with salt and mix it with the coriander.
instructions.2: Cut the beef into small cubes and fry in the oil until it has reabsorbed its juices.
instructions.3: Fry the garlic mixture in a separate pan and add it to the beef.
instructions.4: Season, cover the meat with stock or water and simmer gently for 60–90 minutes.

ec-218.title: Pressed Beef with Onion and Tomato Gravy (Kanduza)
ec-218.culturalNotes: Recipe 218, page 97 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Slice the beef 2 cm thick and pound to tenderise.
instructions.2: Layer onions, beef and tomatoes in a pot, seasoning each layer lightly.
instructions.3: Weigh the layers down, add 1 cup of water and cook over a low heat for 30–40 minutes.
instructions.4: Take out the beef, fry it in oil and keep it warm on a serving dish.
instructions.5: Blend the vegetables with their juices, strain, and return to the pot.
instructions.6: Season, stir in the cornflour, cook for 2–3 minutes and pour over the beef.

ec-219.title: Garlic-Studded Pot Roast (Lahma Rustu)
ec-219.culturalNotes: Recipe 219, page 98 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Pierce the meat in several places with the tip of a sharp knife.
instructions.2: Roll each garlic clove in salt and pepper and push it into one of the holes.
instructions.3: Brown the meat all over in hot oil.
instructions.4: Add water to come halfway up the meat and cook until tender.
instructions.5: Chill before slicing.

ec-221.title: Cheese and Parsley Beef Rolls in Onion Gravy (Lahma Mahshiya)
ec-221.culturalNotes: Recipe 221, page 98 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Slice the beef very thinly, cut it into 10 cm squares and pound to tenderise.
instructions.2: Mix the cheeses with the parsley, spread a little on each slice, roll it up and tie with thread.
instructions.3: Put the rolls in a glass or ceramic dish, pour over the blended marinade ingredients and leave for 1–2 hours.
instructions.4: Brush off the marinade (keep it), brown the rolls lightly and arrange them in a baking pan.
instructions.5: Fry the flour in a little oil, take it off the heat and gradually whisk in the strained marinade. Cook for 3–5 minutes and pour over the rolls, adding warm water if the meat is not covered.
instructions.6: Bake in the middle of a moderate, preheated oven for 30 minutes. Snip off the threads before serving.

ec-227.title: Fried Beef and Egg Patties (Kufta bi-l-Beid)
ec-227.culturalNotes: Recipe 227, page 101 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Mince the beef, onion and breadcrumbs together twice, or pound them until smooth.
instructions.2: Beat the eggs with salt and pepper and work them into the meat.
instructions.3: Shape into round patties 5–7 cm across and 2 cm thick.
instructions.4: Fry in oil until browned on both sides and cooked through.

ec-228.title: Garlic Meatballs in Sweet-Sour Tomato Sauce (Kufta bi-l-Toom wi-l-Bassal)
ec-228.culturalNotes: Recipe 228, page 101 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Mince the beef, onion and garlic together twice, or pound until smooth. Season and mix.
instructions.2: Shape into small balls and fry.
instructions.3: Dissolve the vinegar and sugar in the tomato juice and cook for 3–5 minutes.
instructions.4: Drop in the meatballs and simmer for 30 minutes, shaking the pot gently now and then so they do not stick.
instructions.5: Thicken the sauce with the cornflour.

ec-229.title: Leek Meatballs in Lemon Broth (Kufta bi-l-Kurrat)
ec-229.culturalNotes: Recipe 229, page 102 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Boil the leeks in salted water until tender and drain.
instructions.2: Mince the beef and leeks together twice, then mix in the beaten eggs, breadcrumbs, salt and pepper.
instructions.3: Shape into small balls and fry.
instructions.4: Bring 2 cups of water to the boil with 1 tablespoon of oil and the lemon juice.
instructions.5: Slip in the meatballs and simmer for about 30 minutes, shaking the pot gently so they do not stick.

ec-236.title: Lamb Stew with Crisp Potato Fingers (Lahma Dani Matbukha)
ec-236.culturalNotes: Recipe 236, page 105 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the meat into bite-sized cubes. Peel the tomato, garlic and onion.
instructions.2: Cook the meat with the whole vegetables in oil over a very low heat until the juices have been reabsorbed.
instructions.3: Cover with warm water, season and cook over a very low heat for about an hour, until tender.
instructions.4: Lift the meat onto a serving dish and keep warm.
instructions.5: Mash the vegetables into the broth until smooth, bring it to the boil and toss in the fried potatoes. Cook for 3–5 minutes.
instructions.6: Pour over the meat and serve hot.

ec-238.title: Braised Veal Shin with Straw Potatoes (Moza Matbukha)
ec-238.culturalNotes: Recipe 238, page 106 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the meat into bite-sized cubes and slice the onions coarsely.
instructions.2: Sauté the onions in oil, add the meat and brown it all over.
instructions.3: Cover with warm water, season and cook over a very low heat for about an hour.
instructions.4: Cut the peeled potatoes into matchsticks, fry until very crisp and drain on absorbent paper.
instructions.5: When the meat is ready, add the potatoes and cook for about 10 minutes so they soak up the juices.

ec-243.title: Tunisian Lamb and Parsley Tajine (Tajine Ma’doones)
ec-243.culturalNotes: Recipe 243, page 110 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the beans overnight, then boil them in fresh water for 20–30 minutes. Drain, keeping the liquid.
instructions.2: Cut the lamb into bite-sized cubes and roll them in salt and pepper.
instructions.3: Soften the onions in olive oil, add the lamb and fry until its juices have been reabsorbed.
instructions.4: Add the cayenne, beans, tabil and the tomato paste dissolved in enough bean liquid to just cover the lamb. Cook until the lamb and beans are tender, then take off the heat.
instructions.5: Beat the eggs with the parsley, breadcrumbs, cheese and seasoning and stir them thoroughly into the lamb.
instructions.6: Pour into a well-greased ovenproof dish and bake in a moderate oven for 15–20 minutes, until set.

ec-244.title: Tunisian Lamb and Mint Tajine (Tajine Na‘na‘)
ec-244.culturalNotes: Recipe 244, page 110 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the lamb into bite-sized pieces and roll them in salt and pepper.
instructions.2: Fry the onions in ghee until golden, add the lamb and brown it until its juices are reabsorbed.
instructions.3: Stir in the tomatoes, tabil and seasoning and cook over a low heat for 30 minutes, adding hot water if the meat is not covered.
instructions.4: Drain the meat, keeping the broth, and put it in a greased casserole.
instructions.5: Beat the eggs with the cheese, mint, breadcrumbs and seasoning, mix in the meat and 1 cup of the broth, and pour back into the casserole.
instructions.6: Bake in a moderate oven for 20 minutes.

ec-245.title: Cypriot Tava (Lamb and Tomato Slow-Baked with Cumin)
ec-245.culturalNotes: Recipe 245, page 111 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the lamb into bite-sized cubes.
instructions.2: Thin the tomato paste with 1/2 cup of warm water and put it in a casserole with all the other ingredients.
instructions.3: Close with a tight-fitting lid and bake in a moderate oven for 2–3 hours, until the lamb is tender and the sauce has thickened.

ec-246.title: Tunisian Lamb and Potato Meatballs (Kabaar)
ec-246.culturalNotes: Recipe 246, page 111 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Boil the potatoes until very soft, then peel and mash them.
instructions.2: Mince the lamb twice with the onions, garlic, parsley, coriander, salt and pepper.
instructions.3: Mix in the mashed potato, breadcrumbs, cinnamon and well-beaten eggs.
instructions.4: Shape into small balls and chill for 30 minutes.
instructions.5: Fry in very hot oil until browned all over.

ec-247.title: Baked Kofta Rolls with Pine Nuts (Kafta Mabroomeh / Mkabtaleh)
ec-247.culturalNotes: Recipe 247, page 112 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Mince the meat twice with the onions, garlic, salt and pepper.
instructions.2: Beat the eggs, add them to the meat and knead well.
instructions.3: Roll the meat out about 1 cm thick on a lightly greased surface and cut it into rounds.
instructions.4: Put a few pine nuts in the middle of each round and roll it up.
instructions.5: Arrange the rolls on a well-greased tray and brush each with fat.
instructions.6: Bake in the middle of a moderate oven for 30 minutes, then brown under the grill, shaking the tray so they colour evenly.

ec-248.title: Lebanese Kafta Fatteh with Garlic Yogurt (Fatteet Kafta Madqooqa)
ec-248.culturalNotes: Recipe 248, page 112 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Mince the lamb twice with the fresh mint, salt and pepper, and shape into patties.
instructions.2: Fry the patties until nicely browned.
instructions.3: Break the bread into bite-sized pieces and put them in a deep serving bowl.
instructions.4: Mix the yogurt with the garlic and dried mint, then stir in the oil left from frying the patties.
instructions.5: Pour the yogurt over the bread and top with the kafta.
